input.reasoning_summary: The claim asserts that Apple's Q3 FY2026 results (quarter ended June 27, 2026) "were not affected by tariff or trade-related cost pressures." Evidence E15 from the Q3 2026 10-Q explicitly contradicts this assertion by stating that products gross margin increased during the third quarter "primarily due to a different mix of products and tariff refunds." The inclusion of "tariff refunds" as one of the primary drivers of improved gross margin performance demonstrates that tariff-related factors materially affected the quarter's results. Evidence E7 provides context that Apple was applying for tariff refunds following a February 20, 2026 Supreme Court ruling that struck down certain tariffs. The fact that tariff refunds were significant enough to be listed as a primary driver of gross margin improvement (alongside product mix) directly refutes the claim that results were not affected by tariff or trade-related cost pressures. The tariff refunds represent a positive impact from trade-related factors on the quarter's financial performance.
